sec: Invasive prenatal diagnostic procedures: CVS vs amniocentesis
q: Match the procedure with its timing and caveat — 1) Chorionic villus sampling 2) Early amniocentesis before 14 weeks 3) Standard amniocentesis … A) From 15 weeks, the safest window with the lowest loss and talipes risk B) 10-13 weeks, transabdominal or transcervical placental sampling C) Avoided, because it raises pregnancy loss and fetal talipes
exp: CVS is the 10-13 week option, amniocentesis is best from 15 weeks, and amniocentesis before 14 weeks is linked to loss and talipes.

q: Fill up: Cordocentesis is generally performed after ______ weeks and samples blood from the ______.
exp: Cordocentesis (percutaneous umbilical blood sampling) is done after 18 weeks, usually from the umbilical vein.

sec: Antepartum fetal surveillance principles & movement counts
q: Fill up: With the Cardiff count-to-ten chart, the woman reports if she feels fewer than ______ distinct movements in ______ hours.
exp: Fewer than ten fetal movements in 12 hours (or a marked fall from her own baseline) triggers further testing.

q: At 40 weeks a non-stress test shows a baseline of 140 bpm, moderate variability, two accelerations of 15 bpm lasting 15 seconds in a 20-minute window and no decelerations. How is this tracing reported?
opts: Reactive and reassuring — continue routine antenatal care
Non-reactive — extend for 40 minutes and use vibroacoustic stimulation
Equivalent to a positive contraction stress test — deliver the fetus
A sinusoidal pattern — proceed to immediate caesarean delivery
exp: Two accelerations of 15 bpm for 15 seconds in 20 minutes with moderate variability make the NST reactive, which is reassuring.

q: All of the following can produce a sinusoidal fetal heart rate pattern EXCEPT:
opts: Severe fetal anaemia from Rh isoimmunisation
exp: A sinusoidal pattern signals severe anaemia or hypoxia; the fetal sleep cycle reduces variability but never produces a smooth sine wave.

sec: Biophysical profile (BPP / Manning score) & modified BPS
q: Fill up: The full biophysical profile scores ______ components, and a total score of ______ or less is considered abnormal at term.
exp: Five components are scored out of two each; a score of 4 or less is abnormal, 6 is equivocal and 8-10 is reassuring.

q: Which of the following statements about intrapartum fetal surveillance is TRUE?
opts: In low-risk labour, intermittent auscultation every 15 minutes in the first stage is an accepted alternative to continuous CTG
Continuous electronic monitoring is mandatory for every labour, whatever the risk status
Auscultation should be performed for a full minute before a contraction rather than after it
A handheld Doppler device cannot be used for intermittent auscultation in labour
exp: Low-risk labours may be monitored by intermittent auscultation, counting for at least a minute immediately after a contraction.

q: Match the CTG term with its definition — 1) Fetal tachycardia 2) Minimal variability 3) Prolonged deceleration … A) Amplitude range of 5 bpm or less persisting for 40 minutes or more B) Baseline above 160 bpm for 10 minutes or more C) A fall of 15 bpm or more lasting over 2 minutes but under 10 minutes
exp: Tachycardia exceeds 160 bpm for 10 minutes, minimal variability is an amplitude of 5 bpm or less, and a prolonged deceleration lasts 2 to 10 minutes.

sec: Deceleration morphologies: early, late & variable decelerations
q: Match the deceleration with its cause and shape — 1) Early deceleration 2) Late deceleration 3) Variable deceleration … A) Uniform, mirrors the contraction, nadir at the peak, from head compression B) Uniform, nadir after the contraction peak, from uteroplacental insufficiency C) Abrupt V-shaped fall and recovery, from cord compression
exp: Early decelerations mirror contractions from head compression, late decelerations lag behind from placental insufficiency, and variable decelerations are abrupt from cord compression.

q: A labouring woman's CTG shows a baseline of 110 bpm, minimal variability and recurrent late decelerations with no accelerations. How should this tracing be categorised and managed?
opts: Category III — start intrauterine resuscitation and expedite delivery
Category I — normal tracing needing no intervention
Category II — continue monitoring and review again in 30 minutes
Category III — but delivery can safely wait two hours for a trial of rest
exp: Absent or minimal variability with recurrent late decelerations is a Category III tracing, requiring resuscitation and prompt delivery.

sec: Fetal scalp blood sampling, scalp stimulation & pulse oximetry
q: Fill up: Fetal scalp blood sampling is abnormal when the pH is below ______, while a value of 7.20 to 7.25 is ______.
exp: A pH below 7.20 is abnormal and 7.20-7.25 is borderline, so the sample is repeated after resuscitation.

sec: Maternal adaptations: cutaneous, uterine & cervical shifts
q: All of the following are normal skin changes of pregnancy EXCEPT:
opts: Generalised pruritus with jaundice and dark urine
Linea nigra over the lower abdomen
Chloasma or melasma over the cheeks
Striae gravidarum over the abdomen and thighs
exp: Pruritus with jaundice suggests intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy; linea nigra, chloasma and striae are normal.

sec: Vaginal ecosystem, endocrine shifts & fluid retention
q: Which of the following statements about the vaginal environment in pregnancy is TRUE?
opts: Physiological leucorrhoea is increased cervical mucus from oestrogen, and the vaginal pH stays acidic
Vaginal pH rises above 6 in normal pregnancy, which is why bacterial vaginosis is so common
Progesterone dries and thins cervical mucus, reducing the discharge of normal pregnancy
Total body water falls in pregnancy despite the rise in aldosterone and renin
exp: Oestrogen increases cervical mucus and glycogen, keeping the vagina acidic; total body water rises by several litres in pregnancy.

q: Fill up: In pregnancy the plasma volume expands by about ______%, but the red cell mass rises by only about ______%, producing physiological anaemia.
exp: Greater plasma expansion than red cell expansion dilutes the haemoglobin, which is why the physiological nadir occurs around 30 weeks.

q: Match the renal change with its direction in pregnancy — 1) Renal plasma flow and GFR 2) Serum creatinine 3) Ureteric and pelvic dilation … A) Falls to about 0.5-0.7 mg/dL, so a normal non-pregnant value may be abnormal B) Rises by 50-75% in the first half of pregnancy C) More marked on the right, from uterine compression of the ureter at the pelvic brim
exp: Filtration rises, creatinine falls and the right ureter dilates more, which is why pyelonephritis is commoner on the right.
